model.title: SEC Reform and Restructuring Act
model.meta: Financial Services Committee · Rep. Ann Wagner (R-MO)

summary.text: The bill would change how the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) writes and enforces its rules across several areas. It would require the SEC to weigh costs and benefits, and to explain the problem a rule addresses, before adopting new regulations, and to review major rules after they take effect. It would have the SEC chairman testify to Congress every six months, require an independent audit of the SEC's technology and cybersecurity, and direct the SEC to consider the cumulative effect of its rules. It would move oversight of public company auditors from the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board into an office within the SEC, with the board ending two years after enactment. It would also set a minimum 60-day public comment period (30 days when investor harm is imminent), clarify how violations are counted for penalties, and require the SEC chairman to review and reduce the offices reporting directly to him and allow consolidation of regional offices.
